edges.description: Persistent replication in cardiac tissue recruits the infiltrate that produces the myocardial lesion.

The tissue lesion presenting clinically. Myocarditis is the phenotype the myocardial inflammation and injury node produces, and is named as such both in the mouse histology and in the patient literature.
Persistent inflammation of the joint is what patients experience as the arthralgia that defines chikungunya and that outlasts the acute illness.
edges.source: Joint and Muscle Inflammation with Neutrophil Infiltration

evidence.snippet: The disease typically consists of an acute illness characterised by fever, rash, and incapacitating arthralgia.

nodes.description: Chikungunya virus establishes productive replication preferentially in fibroblasts of muscle, joint and skin, a tropism recovered from human biopsy material as well as from the mouse model. This node is the shared root of the entry: the musculoskeletal syndrome and the cardiac arm both begin from infection of the same cell lineage in different tissues.
nodes.id: CHIKV Replication in Fibroblast-Lineage Target Cells

evidence.snippet: CHIKV primarily targets muscle, joint, and skin fibroblasts, a cell and tissue tropism similar to that observed in biopsy samples of CHIKV-infected humans

nodes.description: Chikungunya virus directly infects and actively replicates in cardiac fibroblasts. This is shown in an immunocompetent mouse model and in primary human cardiac cells, so the cardiac arm rests on a demonstrated cell target rather than on the clinical association alone.

evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that CHIKV directly infects and actively replicates in cardiac fibroblasts

nodes.description: Inflammatory cell infiltration of cardiac tissue with focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the great vessels at the base of the heart. Blocking IL-17A signalling reduces the pro-inflammatory mediators, the infiltrate and the injury together, which is the observation that makes this node the endpoint of the IL-17A arm rather than an independent process.

evidence.snippet: In the absence of MAVS signaling, persistent infection leads to focal myocarditis and vasculitis of the large vessels attached to the base of the heart
reduced immune cell infiltration into cardiac tissue, and mitigated cardiac injury
Cardiovascular manifestations can be considered common and have been reported in France, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Colombia, Venezuela and USA

nodes.description: IL-17A is produced locally in chikungunya-infected cardiac tissue. PROVISIONAL because the cardiac localisation rests solely on a preprint: the peer-reviewed human data measure IL-17 in patient sera and the peer-reviewed mouse data measure it in joint and muscle, so neither places the cytokine in the heart.
nodes.id: IL-17A Production in Infected Heart Tissue

evidence.snippet: We found that CHIKV infection induced IL-17A production in the heart
Sera from CHIKV-infected patients who displayed both acute and chronic disease showed high levels of IL-17, IL-6, IL-21, IL-22, and IL-23, especially during the chronic phase of disease

nodes.description: IL-17A signalling through IL-17RA in cardiac tissue. Removing the receptor or blocking it pharmacologically raises the local interferon response and lowers viral burden, so this is the step the emerging hypothesis places upstream of the interferon response rather than downstream of the damage. PROVISIONAL because every result placing IL-17RA signalling in the heart comes from the same preprint.

evidence.snippet: Genetic deletion of IL-17A signaling significantly enhanced type I interferon responses and decreased viral burden in mouse hearts

blockade of IL-17RA with an FDA-approved monoclonal antibody for plaque psoriasis, Brodalumab, drastically increased type I interferon production and reduced viral replication in both human cardiac fibroblasts and human embryonic kidney 293 (HEK 293) cells

nodes.description: Inflammatory infiltration of joint and muscle tissue, with neutrophils prominent, underlying the arthralgia and myalgia of acute chikungunya and persisting into the postacute phase. IL-17A is required for it in the mouse and is elevated in patients, most strongly during chronic disease; that dependence is recorded as evidence on this node rather than as an edge from the cardiac IL-17A nodes, because the peer-reviewed result is about joint and muscle tissue and the cardiac nodes are explicitly localised to the heart.
nodes.id: Joint and Muscle Inflammation with Neutrophil Infiltration

evidence.snippet: CHIKV-infected mice lacking IL-17A showed reduced tissue inflammation and neutrophil infiltration, compared to wild-type mice
These investigations showed a role for IL-17 in the acute phase of CHIKV infection and also during the postacute disease resolution phase

nodes.description: Loss of signalling through the mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein MAVS, the adaptor for cytoplasmic viral RNA sensing. In the model system this state is produced genetically rather than by the virus, which is why it is curated as an upstream host lesion with no incoming edge from infection: the reviewer-suggested route from cardiac infection to sensing failure is not something the source shows. What the source does show is the consequence — mice deficient in MAVS signalling fail to clear chikungunya virus from the heart — so the outgoing edge, not an incoming one, is where the evidence sits. PROVISIONAL because no comparable sensing lesion has been demonstrated in patients with chikungunya cardiac disease.

biological_processes: cytoplasmic pattern recognition receptor signaling pathway

evidence.snippet: Using mice deficient in major innate immunity signaling components, we found that signaling through the mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS) is required for viral clearance from the heart

nodes.description: Myocardial inflammation reported among the cardiovascular manifestations of systemic chikungunya virus infection, alongside arrhythmias, dilated cardiomyopathy and heart failure. No frequency band is asserted: the source that establishes these manifestations occur also states that isolated cardiac compromise is uncommon, and the two statements cannot be reconciled into a band without going beyond what is reported.

evidence.snippet: Cardiovascular manifestations can be considered common and have been reported in France, India, Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Colombia, Venezuela and USA, including mainly, but no limited to: hypotension, shock and circulatory collapse, Raynaud phenomenon, arrhythmias, murmurs, myocarditis, dilated cardiomyopathy, congestive insufficiency, heart failure and altered function profile (Troponins, CPK).

nodes.description: Virus that is not cleared continues to replicate in the myocardium and in the vascular tissue at the base of the heart. In the mouse this persistence is prolonged, with large vessel vasculitis still present two months after infection. Whether human cardiac involvement reflects persistence or a single acute insult has not been established, hence PROVISIONAL.

evidence.snippet: Large vessel vasculitis was observed for up to 60 days post infection, suggesting CHIKV can lead to vascular inflammation and potential long-lasting cardiovascular complications

nodes.description: Clearance of chikungunya virus from the heart depends on a local type I interferon response raised by both infected and uninfected cardiac cells. Anything that blunts that response therefore converts a self-limiting cardiac infection into a persistent one. Two routes to a blunted response reach this node and they differ sharply in standing: loss of MAVS-dependent innate sensing is a peer-reviewed genetic result and has its own upstream node, whereas restraint by IL-17RA signalling is the emerging claim and is marked as such on its incoming edge. The node is PROVISIONAL because interferon insufficiency has not been measured in the hearts of infected humans.
nodes.id: Restrained Cardiac Type I Interferon Response

evidence.snippet: In immunocompetent mice, CHIKV is cleared from cardiac tissue without significant damage through the induction of a local type I interferon response from both infected and non-infected cardiac cells
Genetic deletion of IL-17A signaling significantly enhanced type I interferon responses and decreased viral burden in mouse hearts
